title: It's Green, It's Got A Hood
mood: tipsy and dead serious about a coat
subject: describing your lost coat to the cloakroom attendant at four in the morning without your ticket
caption: Tech house in the current US club style. A dry punchy 909 kick on every beat, sidechained against a mono sub; a dry 909 clap on two and four; a rubbery filter-envelope synth bassline that bends up at the end of each bar and carries the hook; rolling off-beat open hi-hats with swung sixteenth shakers and rimshot ticks; one short minor chord stab every two bars; a snare roll and white-noise riser into a filtered breakdown before the last hook. Dry and tight, narrow low end with the kick and bass forward, hats wide, almost no reverb. Male voice, low and deadpan, half-spoken in the verses and repeating one short half-sung line as the hook, a single live singer with no effects. 126 BPM, G minor. Tipsy and dead serious about a coat. No big sung pop chorus, no trance supersaw, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no afro percussion.
lyrics:
[Intro - short, 909 kick and rubbery bassline]

[Verse 1]
Four a.m. at the cloakroom and I've got no ticket
I had it in my hand, and then I had a mojito
The man behind the counter has a thousand coats
He says "describe it", so I lean in close

[Pre-Chorus]
I say listen, listen
It's not complicated

[Chorus]
It's green, it's got a hood
It's green, it's got a hood
Left pocket, half a Twix and a dry-cleaning tag
It's green, it's got a hood

[Verse 2]
He holds up something green, I say no, that's moss
He holds up something with a hood, I say that's beige
There's a queue behind me now and they're getting into it
A girl in silver shouts "is the hood fur, though?"

[Pre-Chorus]
The hood is not fur
The hood is the hood

[Chorus]
It's green, it's got a hood
It's green, it's got a hood
He's gone into the back with a torch for me
That's it, that's my coat, it's green, it's got a hood

[Outro - bassline alone, kick drops out]
Ticket was in the hood the whole time
Don't tell him
